results.question: What are the prerequisites for Deep Learning (TDIS22)?
results.expected_answer: 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Computer Science/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering, plus completed Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics for Intelligent Systems and Machine Learning (7.5 credits each) or equivalent; English proficiency.
results.answer: To take Deep Learning (TDIS22), you need passed courses of at least 90 credits within the major subject Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from the Computer Science and Engineering programme. You must also have completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits), Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), and Machine Learning (7.5 credits) or equivalent, and provide proof of English proficiency. [1]

results.question: How is TARI29 graded?
results.expected_answer: 5, 4, 3 or U; final grade only after all assessments are completed.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits) is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. The final grade is based on a balanced set of assessments and is only issued after satisfactory completion of all assessments, namely the Examination (5 credits) and the Assignment (2.5 credits), each graded 5/4/3/U [1].

results.question: What grading scale does the Communication and Artificial Intelligence course use?
results.expected_answer: A, B, C, D, E, FX or F; A to E are passing grades.
results.answer: The Communication and Artificial Intelligence course (LAIK15) is graded A, B, C, D, E, FX or F, with A to E as passing grades [1]. The similarly named Communication and AI course (L1CAAM) uses the same scale [3]. Group presentations are graded U/G rather than on the A-F scale in both courses [4][5]. Other courses may differ.

results.question: What do I need before taking Mathematical Statistics?
results.expected_answer: General entry requirements and completed Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits, or equivalent.
results.answer: You need general entry requirements and the completed course Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits (or the equivalent) for Mathematical Statistics (TMSK17) [1].

results.question: How is the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence course examined?
results.expected_answer: Active participation in seminars and group discussions, and three assignments; graded 5, 4, 3 or U.
results.answer: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (TAIR22) course is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. Examination consists of active participation in seminars and group discussions, plus three assignments: an investigation of a fairness-related ethical challenge in a practical case, a group presentation debating an ethical topic, and a written debate assignment. The final grade requires satisfactory completion of all assessments.

results.question: How is the final project in computer science examined?
results.expected_answer: Written report, oral presentation, opposition on another group's work, and mandatory elements; graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail.
results.answer: The Final Project Work in Computer Science has two current syllabi with similar examination forms. Under TEXT25 (2025), it is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, and opposition to another group's report, with a grade given only after all parts are passed [1]. Under TEXV23 (2024), it is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, review and discussion of another group's work, and fulfilment of mandatory elements, graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail [3]. Other courses may differ, so specify the course name and code for an exact answer.

results.question: Does the Deep Learning course include a project?
results.expected_answer: Yes: one project with tutoring and two project seminars (design and final presentation).
results.answer: Yes. The Deep Learning course (TDIS22) includes one project, with project tutoring and two project seminars [1]. The Deep Learning for PhD Students course (FT3DLFP) also includes one project, with project tutoring and two project seminars [3]. Since your question does not name a course, these rules come from those two courses, and other courses may differ.

results.question: Which language is the Artificial Intelligence course TARI29 taught in?
results.expected_answer: English.
results.answer: The Artificial Intelligence course (TARI29) is taught in English [1].

results.question: What topics does TARI29 cover?
results.expected_answer: Traditional AI and search, reasoning under uncertainty, evolutionary optimization, intelligent agents, game theory and minimax, Markov decision processes.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, current version) covers traditional AI (GOFAI) topics such as problem representation, production systems, search, planning, expert systems, automated reasoning, propositional and predicate logic, and resolution [1]. It also covers reasoning under uncertainty (Bayesian inferencing), programming an evolutionary optimization solution, intelligent agents, basic game theory with minimax, and agents for Markov decision processes [1].

results.question: What are the entry requirements for Mathematics for Intelligent Systems?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, IT or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, including at least 15 credits of mathematics.
results.answer: For Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (TMAR21), applicants must hold a minimum of a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, Information Technology or Electrical Engineering (with relevant computer engineering courses), or equivalent. The bachelor's degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required.

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work in Computer Science (TEXV23) be waived?
results.expected_answer: The programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements, but not from the required Bachelor degree.
results.answer: Yes, the programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements under Prerequisites for TEXV23 [1]. The required Bachelor degree cannot be waived [1]. The points requirements are at least 75 credits of second-cycle courses, including research methodology, and 21 credits of mathematics from first cycle [4].

results.question: When can I start my final project work?
results.expected_answer: After the examiner's approval.
results.answer: Under the general rules for final project work, you can start once the registration form and project description are approved by the examiner, and you meet the prerequisites in your course syllabus [3][5]. Several course syllabi also state that you may start after examiner approval, for example Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25) [1], Final Project Work in Production Systems (TEPV25) [2], and Final Project Work in Product Development (TETT23) [4]. Your question does not name a course, so other courses may differ. Check your own course syllabus for its specific prerequisites.

results.question: Which courses must I have taken before Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving?
results.expected_answer: Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, among the listed courses, plus 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: For Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving (TIOS26), you need at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering with relevant Computer Engineering courses, or equivalent. Alternatively, you need at least 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering, plus Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Knowledge Representation and the Semantic Web (7.5 credits), or equivalent. Proof of English proficiency is also required.

results.question: How is the final grade decided in Deep Learning?
results.expected_answer: Graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail; project credits come from the report, two presentations and active participation in two seminars.
results.answer: In Deep Learning (TDIS22), the course is graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail, and the final grade is determined by the two presentations and the project report [1]. The grade for the report is based on both its collaborative and individual parts [1]. The final course grade is issued only when all course units have been passed [2].

results.question: What kind of teaching does Data Science Programming have?
results.expected_answer: Lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, in English.
results.answer: Data Science Programming (TDPS22) teaching consists of lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, and is conducted in English [1].

results.question: What happens if I am late to my exam?
results.expected_answer: Doors are closed and locked 10 minutes before the exam starts; be on site no later than 10 minutes before.
results.answer: If you arrive after the doors lock 10 minutes before the exam, you will not be admitted until the second admission, 30 minutes into the exam (9:30 AM or 2:30 PM). An invigilator will check your ID and give brief instructions, and you will get your seat number. If you arrive more than 30 minutes late, you will not be allowed to take the exam, and no excuses are accepted.

results.question: How many days before an exam must I register?
results.expected_answer: No later than 10 days before; unregistered students cannot take the exam.
results.answer: You must register for your examination no later than 10 days before the examination date. Students who have not registered in time are not entitled to attend the examination. [1][2]

results.question: Which IDs are accepted at exams?
results.expected_answer: Valid Swedish driver's license, Swedish passport, Swedish national ID card, or JU card marked Identity Card; valid foreign passports under conditions.
results.answer: Accepted IDs for exams are a valid Swedish driver's license, a valid Swedish passport, a valid Swedish national ID card, or a valid JU card marked "Identity Card" [1]. Foreign passports must be valid, plastic wrapped, and in English, French, or Spanish [1]. BankID and Freja eID+ are not accepted because they are not physical identification [1].

results.question: Can I identify myself with BankID at an exam?
results.expected_answer: No. BankID and Freja eID+ are not physical identification.
results.answer: No. BankID does not count as physical identification, so it is not accepted as a valid ID for exams. You must show an accepted physical ID, such as a valid Swedish driver's license, passport, national ID card, or a JU card marked "Identity Card".

results.question: Can I bring snacks into the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Food and drinks are allowed, but no nuts, smelly or smudging food, and no fragrances.
results.answer: Yes, you can bring food and drinks into the examination halls, but not nuts or foods containing nuts, and not food that smells or smudges. Only permitted aids, ID, and food or drinks may be on your desk.

results.question: When am I allowed to leave the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Not during the first 30 minutes.
results.answer: You are not allowed to leave the exam hall during the first 30 minutes [1]. After that, leaving without an invigilator's permission cancels your exam, except for restroom visits, which must follow the posted rules (e.g., logging on the restroom list and, if restrooms are outside the hall, only one student leaving at a time) [1][2]. When time is up, you must stop writing and complete the submission process, including ID check [4].

results.question: How long does it take to get my exam results?
results.expected_answer: Results are reported via Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam, except for special reasons.
results.answer: Exam results are normally notified to students through Ladok no later than 20 working days after the examination occasion. If special reasons exist, results may be notified later, but no later than 14 days before the next examination occasion for the course, and students must be notified in writing of the delay.

results.question: Can I keep my student accommodation during a study break?
results.expected_answer: No.
results.answer: No. During a study break (approved leave from studies), the student is not allowed to keep their student accommodation [1].

results.question: What does a study break mean for my residence permit?
results.expected_answer: JU informs the Migration Agency, which revokes the residence permit, so the student must leave Sweden.
results.answer: If you are granted a study break, Jönköping University informs the Swedish Migration Agency, which will revoke your residence permit, so you must leave Sweden [1]. Before applying, it is recommended that you meet with your degree programme's study counsellor to understand these consequences [1].

results.question: What disciplinary measures can be taken against a student?
results.expected_answer: Warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension; expulsion is also possible.
results.answer: The disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension [3]. A warning is given in writing, exclusion from examinations applies for a continuous period of no more than six months, and suspension applies for no more than six months in total [3]. The Committee can also expel a student, meaning they may not continue their education until further notice [3].

results.question: Which decisions can I appeal to the Board of Appeals?
results.expected_answer: Disciplinary Committee decisions (warning, suspension, expulsion) and listed faculty/school decisions.
results.answer: Decisions that can be appealed include Disciplinary Committee decisions to impose a warning or suspension, or to expel a student [1]. Faculty decisions made through the Study Administration can also be appealed, such as rejecting an applicant for not meeting entry requirements, refusing an exception to entry requirements, refusing deferred enrolment, decisions on credit transfer, refusing a degree or course certificate (except for indefinite suspension due to unpaid tuition fees), and withdrawing admission due to incorrect information from the applicant [1]. Also appealable are refusals of exemption from a compulsory element, refusals of leave from studies, withdrawal of a doctoral student's supervision rights, and decisions under Chapter 4, Section 18 of the Discrimination Act [1]. Refusals of tuition fee refunds based on special circumstances are appealable as well [2].

results.question: How do I pay the application fee for a local admission?
results.expected_answer: To JU, by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) via the web payment system.
results.answer: For local admissions, the application fee is paid to JU, either by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) through the web-based payment solution in the online application form, or in another manner agreed with JU. It must be paid no later than the deadline for supplementary information. If you already paid the UHR fee for central admission, you must submit a receipt to JU when applying.

results.question: What does § 5 of the disciplinary committee instructions say?
results.expected_answer: The disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension.
results.answer: Section 5 lists three disciplinary measures: warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension [1]. A warning is a written notice of the Committee's decision [1]. Exclusion from examinations bars participation in University examinations for a continuous period of up to six months, while suspension bars attending classes, examinations, or other education activities for up to six months in total and may apply to certain facilities [1]. Every warning, exclusion, or suspension decision must state its grounds [1].

results.question: What does section 2.15 of the education regulations say about grades?
results.expected_answer: Results are notified via Ladok within 20 working days of the examination.
results.answer: Section 2.15 says exam results must be notified to students through Ladok within 20 working days of the examination, or later for special reasons but no later than 14 days before the next exam occasion, with written notice of the delay. The examiner is responsible for reporting results to Ladok. Feedback on examined elements must be offered no later than 14 days before the next ordinary exam, and equal treatment should be considered when designing examinations.

results.question: What are the TARI29 entry requirements?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering, or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: Applicants need at least a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering (or equivalent), or at least 150 credits from the Computer Science and Engineering programme. The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required.

results.question: What is LAIK15 about?
results.expected_answer: Media and communication and artificial intelligence, including representations of AI and generative AI in media.
results.answer: Communication and Artificial Intelligence (LAIK15) is a 7.5-credit first-cycle course in Media and Communication Science. It covers research perspectives on AI, media and cultural industries, generative AI as a tool for producing texts, and representations of AI [4][3]. Students learn to describe these representations and explain how generative AI is used in media and communication contexts, and to critically reflect on its opportunities and limitations [5][1].

results.question: Is TDPS22 taught in English?
results.expected_answer: Yes.
results.answer: Yes. The teaching in Data Science Programming (TDPS22) is conducted in English [1].

results.question: What does § 28 of the disciplinary committee instructions allow?
results.expected_answer: A decision may always be appealed to the Board of Appeals if it contravenes the Discrimination Act.
results.answer: Section 28 allows a decision of the Disciplinary and Expulsion Committee to always be appealed to the Board of Appeals, on the grounds that the decision contravenes specified provisions of the Discrimination Act (2008:567).

results.question: Can I take Machine Learning (TMLS22) if my major is Computer Science?

You also need completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), or equivalent, plus proof of English proficiency.

You also need completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits), Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), and Machine Learning (7.5 credits) or equivalent, plus proof of English proficiency [1].

results.question: How is Ethics of AI examined this year?

results.question: How many re-exam attempts do I get?
results.expected_answer: Re-exam rules are set per course; the answer must say which course(s) its rule comes from.

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work be waived?
results.expected_answer: Depends on the programme; usually the programme manager can grant an exemption, but not from the Bachelor degree. Must name the course(s).
results.answer: Yes, in some cases. The rules come from individual course syllabi, and each differs. In Final Project Work in Informatics (TWIP17), the course coordinator can exempt students from the credit requirements under Prerequisites [2]. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25), Production Systems (TEUT23), and Informatics (TEIT22), the programme manager can grant such an exemption [1][3][4]. Other courses may differ, and in TEXT25, TEIT22, and Built Environment (TEBV24) no exemption is made to the required Bachelor degree [1][4][5].
